name: Ryokan Ashgrey Slub Henley
description:
Ryokan is a small-batch label operating out of a workshop in the Midmarket district, making garments that sit at the intersection of Japanese workwear restraint and the kind of soft, worn-in quality associated with American heritage clothing — a combination that feels natural in a city where cultural boundaries dissolved long ago. The Ashgrey Slub Henley is their signature piece: a three-button henley in a slubby cotton-analog that has an irregular, slightly textured surface suggesting handmade without claiming it. The fit is relaxed through the chest and shoulders, slightly tapered at the waist. The grey is not a clean grey — it has depth, warmth, the quality of something that was once another color and has arrived here through time.

It's the kind of shirt that people who care about clothes recognize immediately and people who don't care about clothes never notice. The stitching is tight, the seams are clean, the collar won't deform. Ryokan makes two hundred of these per season. They sell out in days. No advertising.
what_it_says: You know what you're looking at. You don't need to explain it to anyone who doesn't.
worn_by: people with strong opinions about fabric
anyone who found Ryokan through a friend who found them through another friend
story_hooks: Ryokan's founder has been offered corponation buyouts four times. Each time he's declined. After the last offer, his workshop's lease was quietly not renewed. He's been operating month-to-month from a secondary location he won't disclose.

A specific run of Ashgrey Henleys from the 2198 season has a dye lot error that makes them a very slightly different shade — almost imperceptible, but wearers can tell. This run has become sought-after.
Someone is wearing a Ryokan Ashgrey Henley in a photograph taken at a crime scene. The shirt is real. The person wearing it has no documented identity.

physical_description.visual_profile: A relaxed yet intentional henley with subtle Japanese minimalism meeting American workwear heritage. The silhouette reads as effortlessly lived-in—not precious, not trying. On-body, it suggests someone who understands restraint and quality over statement.
physical_description.fit: Relaxed through chest and shoulders with a gentle taper at the waist. Not oversized, not fitted—a confident middle ground that flatters without clinging or drowning.
physical_description.primary_material: Cotton-analog slub weave—synthetic or lab-grown with the irregular texture of natural fiber variation, suggesting artisanal production without affectation.
physical_description.texture: Slubby surface with intentional irregularities. Slightly nubby to the touch, catching light unevenly. Soft from wear-in but substantial enough to hold structure. Not smooth; deliberately imperfect.
physical_description.color_scheme: Ashgrey—a warm, depth-filled grey with undertones suggesting age and previous lives. Not sterile or cool-toned. Appears to shift slightly depending on light, suggesting natural dye or complex pigment layering.
physical_description.closures: Three-button henley front placket. Buttons appear substantial, likely bone or ceramic composite. Friction-fit, no zippers.
distinctive_features: Three-button henley placket with reinforced stitching
Visible slub texture throughout indicating quality fiber
Tight, precise seaming suggesting small-batch construction
Collar engineered to resist deformation over time
Subtle Japanese tailoring restraint in proportions
No visible branding or labels from distance
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 2-3 crossover. Priced and positioned as accessible luxury—recognizable to those who seek quality, invisible to mass-market consumption.
physical_description.cultural_context: Signals someone with cultural sophistication, Japanese-influenced aesthetic sensibility, and appreciation for craft. Not corpo-flashy; not street-salvage. Independent, discerning, possibly creative sector or skilled tradework.
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine to broken-in. Even new, reads as naturally aged. Will develop character with wear—color deepening, fabric softening, minor pilling in high-stress areas that only adds to its mythology.
